part1_root_cause.layer_A_committed_index_stale: site/static-data/index.json as COMMITTED in git (every commit since 73afbf9, incl. HEAD 265a7b4) lists ONLY ['VOICE'] — it was generated once from the staged voice.sqlite3 alone and committed as a demo. Meanwhile CI's generate_static.py regenerates index.json at each deploy by scanning ONLY /bible-sources/ (10 files, voice absent), so the DEPLOYED index.json lists the 10 versions and OMITS VOICE. Git and the live site therefore disagree in opposite directions, and the stale committed voice/ tree silently rides along in every Pages deploy. This is the 'silent discovery/indexing gap' — the top-level index is NOT a faithful mirror of the per-version trees that actually exist.
part1_root_cause.layer_B_homepage_empty_state: site/app.js loadVersions() calls ONLY the Worker API /api/v1/versions first and only falls back to /static-data/index.json if the API throws or returns zero versions. Because D1 was mid-import / quota-gated, the API could hang or return an incomplete set; the homepage 'library is being stocked' empty state (renderHome shows it when state.versions.length === 0) is gated on that API result. A stalled workers.dev fetch (no rejection) was reproducibly what a real-browser load hit. The static mirror was wired into per-chapter Reader fetch but NOT reliably into the top-level 'do we have any content' decision.
part1_root_cause.fix_direction: Single source of truth: move voice.sqlite3 into /bible-sources/, regenerate the FULL index.json (all 11 versions incl. VOICE) from /bible-sources/, commit that canonical index, and make BOTH the homepage and the Worker read from the same static tree. Add a CI check that fails loudly if any .sqlite in /bible-sources/ has no corresponding static entry (and vice-versa), so the index can never silently diverge from the source files again.

architecture_decision.worker_static_source: PENDING (task-06 will finalize). Chosen approach: the Worker fetches the static JSON tree from the deployed Pages origin at request time (option A in the contract), with a small in-Worker cache. Rationale: zero duplication of the 60MB+ JSON tree into the Worker bundle (Workers asset-size limits make bundling the full tree impractical), single canonical copy of the data on Pages, free-tier friendly. Documented fully in task-06.
architecture_decision.response_shape_contract: All /api/v1/* routes must return byte-for-byte identical response SHAPES to the pre-migration D1 Worker. Golden reference responses captured (versions, books, book, chapter, verse, search, random) before any change.
